title: Throughput escrow and soft-rotation protocol for Dedicated fleets
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Design and implement a soft-rotation protocol that lets us evict or replace hosts in Dedicated fleets while guaranteeing per-tenant throughput commitments. The approach uses a transient 'throughput escrow' token system and staged preheat windows for KV/cache warming so that rolling maintenance and upgrades do not violate tail-latency or throughput SLOs. Deliver a controller that coordinates: escrow issuance, token-funded traffic shifts, preheat RPCs to warm KV caches, and automatic rollback if throughput dips below thresholds. Provide operator controls for policy (max parallel rotations, escrow size per tenant, maintenance blackout windows) and expose metrics and tracing for post-mortem and capacity accounting.
acceptance_criteria: Controller can allocate escrow tokens per tenant and consume them to shift traffic without user-visible SLO violations
Staged preheat reduces cold-KV tail incidents by >= 70% in synthetic stress tests
Automatic rollback triggers within 15s of throughput regression and restores previous host(s)
Admin UI/CLI shows active escrows, in-flight rotations, and per-rotation telemetry
End-to-end e2e tests in staging exercising parallel rotations (N=3) pass under realistic load generator
comments: 2026-03-02 - Kickoff: scoped initial MVP to support per-tenant escrow tokens + single-host rotating flow. Driving constraints: keep latency perturbation < 5% p95 and avoid tenant throttling during rotate.

2026-03-04 - Architecture review with Runtime and Autoscaler teams. Agreed to implement escrow as a lightweight lease in Redis with monotonic counters; Autoscaler will be responsible for creating temporary capacity lanes when escrow depleted. Action: Diego to prototype lease format and APIs.

2026-03-06 - Prototype PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/5292 created for escrow lease service + basic rotation controller. Initial load test shows KV cache warmup reduced p99 by ~45% but p95 unchanged — investigation ongoing for batching behavior during preheat.

2026-03-09 - Decision: use two-phase preheat: (1) lightweight prefix-warm RPC that only populates KV headers and (2) follow-up full warm for hot seqs. Rationale: avoids heavy prefetch that hurts co-tenants during large migrations.
2026-03-11 - UX: PM requested operator-facing knobs for 'escrow grace fraction' and 'parallel rotation cap'. Added to API surface; docs stub at drive.redwood.com/dedicated/escrow-protocol-v1.

2026-03-13 - Staging run #3: ran 2 rotations concurrently for three medium tenants. Observed a 12% throughput dip for one tenant tied to shared kernel eviction on host. Mitigation: add soft rate-limiter that ramps traffic off host gradually using token burn schedule. Follow-up task created (ENG-140457).

2026-03-14 - Current: controller MVP merged behind feature flag. Next steps: expand e2e test matrix, finalize operator runbook, and schedule canary on a non-critical fleet next week. Link to PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/5348
follow_up_tasks: Canary deploy on staging fleet and capture telemetry for 48h
Coordinate with Console to add visualization for escrow tokens and rotation traces
